A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TESSERA and retain matching methods, application datasets, and figures. The main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original crop-classification, canopy-height, biomass, wildfire-embedding, and stocking-index results, alongside a training-stability comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original application results and adds baseline comparisons, model-scaling experiments, and component ablations.

M1.justification: Figure 1 and Appendix A.5 revise the reported encoder depth from eight Transformer blocks to four. The dual Sentinel-1/2 encoders, MLP fusion, 128-dimensional embeddings, quantization, and Barlow Twins plus mixup objective remain. This is a limited architectural revision; the PDFs do not establish whether it reflects retraining or correction of the earlier description.

E1.justification: The reported global pretraining corpus and five evaluated settings remain: Austrian crops, Borneo canopy heights, Finnish biomass, two California burn regions, and Brazilian agroforestry plots. Scaling and ablation experiments reuse Austrian crops. Newly documented land-cover aids support existing tasks; Appendix J presents a Cambridge tool demonstration without an additional habitat-classification evaluation.

E2.justification: Google Satellite Embedding is added to crop pixel classification, few-shot learning, segmentation, canopy-height, and biomass comparisons. A Sentinel-2 annual-median-composite UNet baseline is also added for canopy height. These additions substantially expand the evaluated comparator set across several principal applications.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: pretraining batch size increases from 8,192 to 32,768; canopy-height patches change from 64x64 to 32x32; and patch-based comparator encoders change from frozen to fine-tuned. BioMassters label subsets are now selected before the 80:20 training/validation split. New scaling and ablation protocols introduce architecture sweeps and RankMe evaluation. These reported revisions do not establish that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices B-C add projector-depth/width and compute-scaling experiments, plus ablations of shuffling, mixup, Sentinel-1 inputs, and quantization. Figure 11 adds qualitative crop-segmentation comparisons. The earlier shuffling-stability analysis remains, while Figure 3 removes the canopy-height binned-bias analysis and example prediction maps.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 2c newly specifies few-shot repetition counts, from 2,000 for one-shot to 100 for twenty-shot; v1 only stated multiple runs. Biomass Figure 4 newly reports averages over five random splits and minimum-maximum ranges. The canopy-height twelve-run evaluation and its uncertainty reporting already appeared in v1.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new comparators, scaling experiments, and ablations; Table 4 reports F1 of 0.773 for the full model versus 0.626 without shuffling and mixup. Existing values also change: PRESTO's crop-embedding Davies-Bouldin index changes from 11.656 to 14.136, and ETH global canopy RMSE from 20.17 to 20.28 m. Biomass curves are replaced under revised protocols, so their lower errors are not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C introduces a formal definition of the new RankMe diagnostic using normalized entropy of normalized embedding singular values, Equation 12. The existing Barlow Twins/mixup mathematics and clustering-metric definitions remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution of global annual pixel embeddings and evaluation on five applications remains. The abstract qualifies broad outperformance as closely matching or outperforming baselines. The introduction adds an explicit combined-property novelty claim and distinguishes the reported 2024 release from the intended 2017-2024 coverage.

C2.justification: Appendices B-C add substantive interpretations concerning scaling, the importance of shuffling and mixup, modest Sentinel-1 benefits, and the accuracy/storage tradeoff of quantization. New discussion addresses compute limits and assumes short-term canopy stability despite reference-date mismatches. The stocking-index section also newly attributes its superior performance specifically to embedding efficiency.

D1.justification: v2 adds parameter and hyperparameter tables and detailed canopy, fire, biomass, and stocking-index procedures in Appendices F-I. Reported pretraining resources change from 3,000 GPU-hours on eight MI300X GPUs to 6,200 on sixteen. Previously intended releases gain concrete GEOTESSERA retrieval and integrity-checking instructions, model/code access information, and disclosure that Brazilian plot data require a Data Transfer Agreement.

R1.justification: Table 5 adds an extensive model-by-feature survey supporting a new explicit positioning claim about TESSERA's combination of openness, ready-to-use outputs, scale, and temporal pixel features. Numerous works are newly cited, including GSE, AnySat, Galileo, and RankMe. This substantially expands research positioning beyond v1's introductory literature discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, encoder/projector explanations are consolidated, duplicate crop subsections are merged, and biomass precedes wildfire analysis. Existing methods are reorganized into dedicated appendices, while acknowledgments and availability information move before them. Terminology shifts broadly from representations and Model-as-Data to embeddings and Embeddings-as-Data.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3 are redrawn or substantially reorganized, and the biomass figure gains additional comparison panels and uncertainty displays. New figures show scaling, crop predictions, and the interactive tool; new tables cover architecture, hyperparameters, ablations, and research positioning. Fire maps, stocking-index plots, and training/shuffling graphics are retained despite relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the method through controlled component/scaling experiments and additional baselines, addressing important evidential gaps in v1. Dedicated application appendices, access instructions, and biomass uncertainty reporting also materially improve reproducibility and assessment. These gains outweigh the removed canopy diagnostics, although conflicting fire years and RH95 versus RH90 stocking-index targets leave unresolved reproducibility problems.
